summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide a tax credit of $1,500 to employers for each additional employee participating in a qualified apprenticeship program, and directs the Office of Management and Budget to reduce government printing costs and establish guidelines for federal publications.

scores.thoughts: Section 3 of the bill explicitly aims to reduce government printing costs by transitioning to digital publications and establishing guidelines for employee printing. This directly targets a reduction in government expenditures.
The primary purpose of this bill is to create a new tax credit for employers who hire apprenticeship employees. This credit reduces the tax liability for businesses, effectively lowering their taxes.

The bill's core provision creates a new non-refundable tax credit of $1,500 per qualifying apprentice (limited to two years), which reduces federal revenue and increases the deficit to support apprenticeship expansion. Section 3's minor printing-cost reductions are secondary and unrelated to the apprenticeship focus, so they do not offset the primary fiscal effect.
